subject: Post-demo recap & proposed hyperscaler vs Redwood benchmark for embeddings/rerank
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@datafoundry.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@datafoundry.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & proposed hyperscaler vs Redwood benchmark for embeddings/rerank

Emma / Amit — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

- Goal we heard: replace current vector search layer to improve recall@10 for support tickets while lowering serving cost. Also need predictable retrieval latency (< 40ms p50) under steady load (200 qps).
- Current stack: in-house FAISS + an embeddings API (hyperscaler) feeding 1536-d vectors. Team cares about latency, cost per query, and how reranking affects top-K precision.

Proposed next steps (we can run these in parallel):
1) Benchmark plan: run a controlled comparison between DataFoundry's current hyperscaler embeddings + FAISS rerank vs Redwood embeddings (512- and 1536-d options) + Redwood rerank path. Focus metrics: recall@1/5/10, retrieval latency p50/p95, tokens/embedding unit cost, and end-to-end RPC latency at 200 qps.
2) Test config: we'll provide a small harness and suggested scripts (attached "proposed-benchmark-config.yaml"). Ideally you give us a representative 10k query set + index snapshot (we can obfuscate if needed).
3) Timing: target 5 business days for initial runs; results + actionable config suggestions after that.

Differentiators we'll measure for you: continuous batching latency profiles, prefix caching of KV for repeated queries, and Redwood's quantized 8-bit embedding path that reduces inference cost without linear degradation in recall.

Attachments: "redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison_v1.pdf" (high-level bullets) and the YAML harness.

If that plan looks good, I can get Rishi to author the exact command-line steps and schedule a quick handoff call.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
+d 415-555-0123

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@datafoundry.com>

Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed hyperscaler vs Redwood benchmark for embeddings/rerank

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we share data: 

- We can produce a 10k obfuscated query set and a snapshot of our FAISS index. ETA for that is end of day Friday (2026-05-14).
- Important constraint: our infra team insists on runner-side isolation — they want the benchmark to be run in our VPC if possible. Is Redwood's private deployment able to run the harness in our environment or do you need us to push sample data to Redwood infra?
- Also: can you confirm the exact vector dims you'll test (you mentioned 512 & 1536) and whether the 512 option is Redwood-trained or a distilled projection of the 1536 vectors?

If you can answer those two things we can greenlight.

—Emma
Emma Johnson
Head of Search & Relevance | DataFoundry

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@datafoundry.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed hyperscaler vs Redwood benchmark for embeddings/rerank

Emma — quick technical clarifications and options: 

1) Runner location: we support two modes for this kind of test: (A) Redwood-managed ephemeral runner in our secure environment (we can do obfuscation on ingest and we sign an NDA); (B) Redwood Private (customer-run) where we deliver a lightweight Docker harness you execute inside your VPC. Given your isolation constraint, option B is recommended — the harness will stream only metrics and anonymized aggregates back to us, no raw vectors leave your VPC. We provided the Dockerfile + scripts in the attached YAML.

2) Vector dims and models we'll test: 
- 1536-d: this is a 3rd-party open checkpoint similar to what you currently use; we'll test as a "like-for-like" baseline.
- 512-d: this is a Redwood-distilled projection trained via our student-teacher pipeline to preserve recall for top-K retrieval while cutting dimensionality (and cost). We'll run both dense retrieval + rerank (lexical + dot-product hybrid).

3) Rerank path: Redwood's recommended flow is (a) retrieve top-200 candidates via ANN, (b) rerank top-20 with cross-encoder (cheap single-pass scoring) and return top-10. We'll measure recall@1/5/10 after rerank and raw retrieval recall.

4) Latency targets & measurement: we'll capture p50/p95 retrieval latency for both the ANN stage and end-to-end rerank call at 200 qps. We'll also simulate 1% burst to test tail behavior.

5) Cost model: we'll output a cost per 10k queries using current hyperscaler pricing you supplied and Redwood's 512/1536 emission costs; we'll include approximate infra cost (GPU seconds) for the rerank step.

If you confirm that you want us to proceed with the inside-vpc harness (option B) we'll send the Docker image + quick runbook.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma — great, thanks for the quick confirm. Option B (harness inside your VPC) is fine. Next operational items: 

- Emma / Amit: please share the obfuscated 10k queries + index snapshot to the secure S3 bucket we provided in the Drive link. If there's a blocker, upload to your internal artifact repo and give our harness read-only access.
- Rishi: please attach the Docker image name + run commands and a short checklist for our infra contact (we'll only need a single EC2 with GPU for the rerank stage; config is in the YAML).
- Neha: I'll schedule a 30-min check-in for Tue 2026-05-19 to review preliminary numbers.

Emma, I'll also include a two-slide summary comparing expected cost deltas (512 vs 1536) and retrieval latency tradeoffs; should help your procurement team.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.

Dylan
